methods.name: Crank–Nicolson
methods.reason: Averages the space difference between the old and new time levels. Each step needs a tridiagonal system solved, but it is stable for every \(r\) and more accurate.

steps.title: Set up the grid
steps.text: Divide the rod into \(N\) intervals and step forward in time. \(u_i^j\) approximates \(u(x_i, t_j)\); the end values are 0.
latex: x_i = i\,\Delta x,\qquad t_j = j\,\Delta t

steps.title: The difference formula
steps.text: Averages the space difference between the old and new time levels. Each step needs a tridiagonal system solved, but it is stable for every \(r\) and more accurate.

steps.title: The mesh ratio
steps.text: Crank–Nicolson is stable for any value of \(r\), so the time step can be chosen for accuracy alone.

steps.title: The system for the first time level
steps.text: The unknowns are the interior values at the new time. The matrix has \(1 + r\) on the diagonal and \(-r/2\) beside it, and is the same at every step.

steps.title: Values on the grid
steps.text: Each row is one time level.
